entries.title: growthpilot-ai
entries.summary: Growth analysis for one real business: a scored diagnosis across 7 dimensions, 19 page checks, and a check of your answers against your own page. Local-first, no account.
entries.body: GrowthPilot A growth analysis for a real business: a scored diagnosis, findings that state their evidence, and a 30/60/90 plan. It opens straight into the app. No account, no sign-in, no server, no database. Live: https://muhammadabubakar69.github.io/growthpilot-ai/ Why it has no backend An earlier version of this project was a multi-tenant SaaS on Supabase with row-level security, auth middleware and a Vercel deployment. It worked, and it was the wrong shape for the job: a business owner had to sign up, confirm an email and create a workspace before seeing anything, and their answers then lived on a server that had to be secured, migrated and paid for. This version keeps the part that matters - the analysis - and removes the part that was friction. The app is a single static page. Your business is stored in your own browser, and the only network request the page ever makes is loading its own files. The three rules the engine follows 1. Nothing is invented. An unanswered dimension is reported as unavailable , never as zero, and no finding is built on a question you skipped. The overall score renormalises over what you actually answered, and shows how complete that is. 2. Every number shows its formula. entries.title: inkplot
entries.summary: Photo to vector halftone in the browser. Dots, squares or diamonds, live tone control, SVG export. No upload, no server.
entries.body: Inkplot Photo to vector halftone, in your browser. Dots, squares or diamonds. Live tone control. Exports clean SVG you can scale, print, or open in Illustrator. No upload, no server, no tracking: every pixel is processed in your tab. Open the studio → Why this exists Halftone portraits are usually either a Photoshop filter (raster, fixed resolution) or a paid web tool that wants your file on its server. Inkplot does the sampling in the browser and emits geometry : circles, rects, diamonds as SVG marks, not a bitmap copy. The output scales to any size, prints at any DPI, and stays editable. It is also the tool behind the dot portrait on my GitHub profile. How it works 1. The image is drawn to a canvas and reduced to one luminance value per pixel, with alpha treated as paper rather than ink. 2. Those values are binned into a grid whose size you control, so density is a live parameter instead of a baking step. 3. Each cell's tone becomes coverage through a gamma and contrast curve, then a mark whose size follows that coverage. Cells below the ink floor emit nothing, so paper stays paper. 4. Marks are written out as SVG. The ASCII button writes the same grid as text. Sampling, tone mapping and mark emission are separate pure functions in src/halftone.ts , which is why the engine is testable without a browser and why the export cannot drift from the preview. entries.title: Power-Digitizing
entries.summary: new design
entries.body: Multi-site platform (Power Digitizing + tenants) One Next.js codebase, many websites. The request hostname selects a site config; components never hardcode a brand. Run Locally every hostname falls back to DEFAULT SITE ID . To test another tenant, use its domain, e.g. add 127.0.0.1 client-001.example.com to your hosts file and open http://client-001.example.com:3000 . How tenants resolve middleware.ts forwards the hostname - lib/tenant.ts matches it against domains in config/sites/ (exact, or .sub.domain.com wildcards) - layout injects theme CSS variables, fonts, metadata and JSON-LD - shared components render that site's data. Add a site 1. Copy config/sites/client-001.ts , change id, domains, theme, content. 2. Register it in config/sites/index.ts . 3. Point the domain at your deployment and add it as a domain in your host (Vercel: Project Domains). The config is validated with Zod at build time; an invalid colour or missing field fails the build. Theme and fonts Colours are tokens ( background , primary , accent , ...) mapped to CSS variables. Fonts are chosen by key from lib/fonts.ts (next/font needs static declarations); add a font there and to FONT KEYS . Not built yet (next steps) Header/hero GSAP and Framer Motion polish, patches/portfolio/blog/process/testimonials/stats sections, service detail pages, quote form with uploads and Resend emails, analytics scripts, legal

entries.title: otto
entries.summary: Autonomous outreach agent with a $0 model bill. No API keys, no subscriptions, no accounts. Standard library only.
entries.body: otto Live site · CI · License: MIT The site has a working demo : it runs a JavaScript port of the pipeline in your browser, and a test asserts its drafts are byte-identical to the Python ones. An autonomous outreach agent with a $0 model bill. No API keys, no subscriptions, no accounts, no free trial that expires. Otto finds businesses worth talking to, reads their website, writes an email that mentions something true about them, queues it for your approval, sends it from your own mailbox, reads the replies, and drafts the answers. It runs on your machine in a loop. Harvey proved the shape of this product. Otto's argument is one step further: you should not have to rent a Claude or ChatGPT plan to run an agent on your own laptop. The agent is Python, the store is SQLite, the model is optional, the bill is zero. --- What it costs --- --- The agent $0, MIT, git clone Finding businesses $0 — a CSV you write, or OpenStreetMap/Overpass (no key) Reading their website $0 — three HTTP requests, no model call Deciding what to do next $0 — four SQL counts Sorting replies $0 — keyword rules Writing the email $0 — built-in templates, or a model you already run locally Sending your own mailbox (Gmail app password works, ~$0) Everything else $0 There is no third provider option on purpose. If it needs a key or a card, Otto does not call it. Why this is fast to run - Zero dependencies. Standa

entries.title: threadmind-ai
entries.summary: Autonomous textile factory intelligence platform: fabric defect vision, predictive maintenance, evidence-grounded root cause analysis, and a five-agent LangGraph orchestrator. Research baseline v1.0.
entries.body: ThreadMind AI Autonomous Textile Factory Intelligence Platform ThreadMind AI is a research platform that connects fabric quality inspection, machine telemetry, production records, and maintenance history into one industrial data layer, then reasons over that layer with specialized ML models and a coordinated multi-agent layer. The question it is built to answer is not only "what defect occurred?" but: What happened, where did it happen, which operational conditions were associated with it, what evidence supports the possible explanation, and what should the responsible engineer investigate next? Status: audited foundation. The security and isolation layer is implemented and tested; models, agents and the dashboard are not. Read docs/repository-audit.md for what is verified versus specified, and docs/production-readiness.md for the gap to operational use. Nothing in docs/ is a claim of achieved model performance. --- What is in the box Component Path State --- --- --- Requirements, audit and reviews docs/ Baseline v1.0 + audit PostgreSQL schema database/schemas/001 initial.sql 24 tables, RLS enforced RLS hardening migration database/migrations/002 rls hardening.sql Implemented + tested FastAPI application layer apps/api Auth, RBAC, errors, telemetry ingest Shared industrial contracts industrial/ Telemetry validation Deterministic telemetry simulator ai-services/telemetry Impleme

entries.title: jobpilot
entries.summary: Track job applications from raw posting text. Offline parser, optional FastRouter/OpenAI extractor, SQLite store, FastAPI + CLI. Live docs on GitHub Pages, image on GHCR.
entries.body: jobpilot Turn a messy job posting into a tracked application, in one command. Live docs : Container : ghcr.io/muhammadabubakar69/jobpilot Most job hunts die in a spreadsheet nobody updates. jobpilot takes the raw text of a posting (an email, a WhatsApp forward, a scraped page) and turns it into a structured record: company, role, salary band, deadline, stack, contact. It runs entirely offline by default, and uses an LLM only when you ask it to. Why it exists Parsing a posting is the tedious part of applying, and the record you need later (what did they pay? when did I apply? did they answer?) is exactly what gets lost. This keeps one SQLite file you own, plus a REST API for anything else you want to point at it. Design Two decisions worth calling out: - The LLM is optional and never trusted blindly. parse with llm validates the JSON, keeps only integers for salary, and merges against the heuristic result, so a hallucinated field falls back to what the regexes actually found. - Deduplication is by fingerprint. Re-importing the same posting is a no-op instead of a duplicate row. Run it Three ways, pick one: The container serves the REST API; docker/build is reproducible because the image pins Python 3.12 and installs the package from pyproject.toml . Quickstart With an LLM extractor Off by default. Set a key and pass --llm : Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works. resolve llm confi
